primary_claim: For a zoo of tiny RNNs (8 to 1,408 parameters) trained on simple algorithmic tasks, ARC achieved a full mechanistic understanding (by surprise accounting) of a 10-parameter model and made substantial but incomplete progress on a 32-parameter model, but could not produce a mechanistic estimate of accuracy competitive with random sampling for a 432-parameter model, illustrating how quickly full mechanistic understanding becomes intractable even at very small scale.

effect.metric: mechanistic estimate quality (mean squared error vs compute / surprise accounting bits) by model size
effect.value: 10-parameter model M_2,2: mechanistic estimate matches empirical error rate to within 1 part in 13,000 using only a handful of operations, with about 40 bits of total surprise, judged a full understanding; 32-parameter model M_4,3: roughly matches sampling's computational efficiency, more-or-less a full understanding though less clear; 432-parameter model M_16,10: failed to produce an estimate competitive with random sampling

contradicts_or_qualifies: Argues the 'ambitious' mechanistic interpretability research program has historically underinvested in fully understanding slightly-complex models relative to partially understanding very complex models, and presents AlgZoo's difficulty fully explaining even a 432-parameter model as evidence of how far that goal is from being achieved.
stated_future_work: Invites other ambitious-oriented researchers to explore the AlgZoo models
Wants to see better mechanistic estimates (mean squared error vs compute) produced for the AlgZoo models
Poses an explicit open challenge: design a method to mechanistically estimate the accuracy of the 432-parameter model M_16,10 that matches random sampling's mean-squared-error-vs-compute performance
Continuing to pursue a scalable, algorithmic approach to producing mechanistic estimates of any quantity of interest, building on ARC's prior 'competing with sampling' work
limitations_stated: Most of the remaining 11 hidden neurons of the 432-parameter model are more densely connected and were not analyzed
No correspondence has been produced between most hidden neurons of the trained 432-parameter model and those of the handcrafted model
The analysis used approximations without accounting for approximation error, which becomes increasingly significant for more complex neurons
Even the brute-force approach judged a full understanding for the smallest model would not scale, since the number of piecewise-linear regions grows exponentially with depth
quote: The largest model that we believe we more-or-less fully understand has 32 parameters; the next largest model that we have put substantial effort into, but have failed to fully understand, has 432 parameters.
